headline: Missing 11-year-old boy found dead
text:
The search for a missing North Forsyth Middle School boy came to a sad end on Thursday when the body of 11-year-old Levi Frady was found in Dawson Forest near an abandoned Lockheed plant.

Friends and neighbors started looking for the boy Thursday morning after his mother, Marilyn Parkman, reported him missing to Forsyth County authorities.

According to Sheriff’s Office reports, Frady left his Burruss Mill Road home Wednesday afternoon to do homework at the Noah Road home of a friend. He was expected back by 6:30 p.m.

Parkman went to the Noah Road home around 7:30 p.m. when Frady had not returned.

The friend’s parents told her Frady had left on his bicycle to eat dinner at another neighbor’s house.

No one was home at that address when Parkman stopped by.

She told Sheriff’s Office investigators she fell asleep after going home, but Frady had not returned when she woke up around 2 a.m. She said she thought he spent the night at another friend’s house.

Friends and neighbors started searching for Frady on Thursday morning.

Frady’s twin sister, Laci, found her brother’s bicycle in a ditch off Little Mill Road, about a half mile from his house. There was no sign of her brother.

Investigators from the Sheriff’s Office, the Georgia State Patrol, the Georgia Emergency Management Agency and Forsyth County EMS and firefighters were called in to help look for the boy Thursday, but were forced to stop looking at dark.

The same day, three hunters from Gilmer County found the body of a young boy in Dawson Forest. On Friday, the body was identified as Frady.

According to Dawson County Sheriff Billy Carlisle, the boy had been shot.

Investigators are questioning family and friends about Frady’s disappearance.

[Continued on page 2A under BOY from 1A]

Carlisle said no one has been arrested in the case, but he said he wants to reassure residents it is not likely there is a random killer of children on the loose.

“I don’t believe there’s any reason to fear that there’s anyone out abducting young boys,” said Carlisle.

But that didn’t calm the fears of Forsyth County parents Friday. Sheriff’s Office deputies reported a dramatic increase in the number of parents picking up their children from school Friday afternoon. North Forsyth Middle School offered counseling to students and faculty to help deal with the situation.

Cumming New Life church has set up a contribution fund for the family. For information on the funds, call Lanier Bank and Trust at 887-1732, Citizens Bank at 886-9500 or Cumming New Life Church at 889-6919.

Frady’s funeral was planned for Sunday at Ingram Funeral Home Chapel. Interment was to be at Sawnee View Garden.

headline: GBI, Dawson County investigating murder
text:
The death of a young Forsyth County sixth grader was no accident. Officials now confirm someone shot the 11-year-old boy and left him to die in a Dawson County forest.

Although Levi Frady was presumably abducted in Forsyth County — probably near the spot where his bicycle was found, authorities say he was murdered a few miles across the line in Dawson County.

“It all happened here,” said Dawson County Sheriff Billy Carlisle Friday afternoon, eliminating speculation that the wooded area off Ga. Hwy. 9 might only have been the murderer’s dumping ground.

When the boy’s assailant is found, Carlisle said, “he or she will be prosecuted here.”

A state crime lab autopsy has confirmed that the young boy died as a result of one or more gunshot wounds, but Carlisle said details of autopsy findings — such as the caliber of the weapon used and the location of the wounds — are not yet available.

He would not confirm whether a possible murder weapon has been found or whether a suspect has been identified, but the sheriff did say no warrants have been issued.

Although Carlisle said agents with the Georgia Bureau of Investigation and Forsyth and Dawson County Sheriff’s Departments have interviewed numerous potential witnesses in the case, he said authorities so far have not felt it necessary to advise anyone

[Continued on page 2A under MURDER from 1A]

of the constitutionally protected right to remain silent during questioning.

However, authorities have not yet been able to talk to everyone close to the boy. Carlisle said authorities are actively searching for Levi’s 34-year-old father, Milton Frady. Carlisle stressed Milton is not considered a suspect in the case.

Instead, Carlisle said the Cumming resident, who is estranged from his son’s mother, is only wanted in connection with previous charges. Carlisle said investigators would like to speak to Milton Frady about his son’s death when he is found.

Before Levi disappeared, Forsyth officials say they held warrants for Milton Frady’s arrest on non-violent charges, including an alleged burglary, a superior court bench warrant and contributing to the delinquency of a minor.

He is described as a 5-feet, 11-inch tall white male, weighing approximately 170 pounds. He has shoulder-length brown hair and hazel eyes.

Parents should not be unduly worried that there is a random child abductor on the loose, Carlisle said: “I don’t think there is a reason to fear that. When something like this happens, statistically speaking, the victim usually knows the perpetrator,” Carlisle said, although he stressed that he is “not saying that is what happened in this case.”

Very little is being divulged about the crime scene itself, and authorities won’t say whether evidence of sexual abuse was discovered. Carlisle also would not say whether the boy was found wearing each item of clothing he was reportedly dressed in when he was last seen: “I will only say that he was clothed.”

Whether other potential evidence was found at the scene, he would not confirm nor deny.

“We don’t want to give out too much information about the crime scene itself to prevent tarnishing the investigation.”

Dawson County officials were called to the scene around 2:30 p.m. Thursday, after three Gilmer County hunters found the body during the opening day of deer season.

Carlisle said members of the hunting party left the scene, near the old Lockheed facility on state wildlife management land and went to a nearby home to make the call to authorities.

When two officers confirmed the report and secured the crime scene, Carlisle said his agents immediately notified the GBI office in Gainesville and requested a crime scene technician be dispatched to the scene.

When Dawson officials realized the boy’s description matched that of the boy reported missing in an earlier radio-broadcasted look-out, they notified Forsyth officials.

Carlisle said his department will continue to work with other state and local agencies to find the person or persons responsible for the homicide.

headline: Levi D. Frady
text:
Levi Dillon Frady, 11, of Cumming, died Thursday, Oct. 23, 1997. Frady was a student at North Forsyth Middle School.

Survivors include his mother, Marilyn Parkman of Cumming; sister, Laci Frady of Cumming; father, Milton Frady of Cumming; grandparents, Dorsey and Janice Hamby and Lamar and Sarah Frady, all of Cumming; great-grandparents, Burma Gibson and Mandy Allene Hamby, both of Cumming; aunts, uncles and cousins.

Funeral services will be held Sunday, Oct. 26, at 2 p.m. at Ingram Funeral Home Chapel. The Rev. David Harris will officiate.

Interment will follow in Sawnee View Garden.

In lieu of flowers, memorial donations may be made to the Levi Dillon Frady Trust Fund at Citizens Bank, 501 Tri-County Plaza, Cumming, Ga. 30040, or Lanier Bank and Trust, 214 Dahlonega St., Cumming, Ga. 30040.

Ingram Funeral Home had charge of the arrangements.

Forsyth County News
October 26, 1997

headline: When tragedy involves the loss of a child, too many questions remain
text:
Why? It’s a difficult question with few consoling answers. Why does a child have to die? And, why so tragic and brutal a death?

No response can ease the pain of the loss felt by the family, by friends, by schoolmates and teachers of Levi Frady, who is to be laid to rest Sunday. No justification can be found for the senseless murder of a child less than a dozen years old. There should have been so much living ahead for the sixth grader.

And the ‘what if’ questions also loom. What if he hadn’t had ridden away on his bike, which was found in a ditch near his home? What if it hadn’t been a school night and what if he hadn’t had homework to do which apparently took him to a friend’s house?

Authorities know a gunshot blast killed the child, but details which have been released are sketchy. Who could have perpetrated such a crime against the bright-eyed youngster? Who would commit such a heinous act — killing and leaving the 11-year-old in the woods?

Whoever is found to be connected to the murder, there is one thing that no one will ever be able to answer to the satisfaction of the family — and the community. Why?

headline: Search for Levi Frady’s killer is continuing
text:
Investigators searching for 11-year-old Levi Frady’s assailant say they have not settled on a suspect in the case, but Dawson County Sheriff Billy Carlisle says agents won’t stop until the person responsible is behind bars.

“We’re still out there working very hard, and we will not quit until this case is solved,” Carlisle said.

Sometime Tuesday police will begin passing out fliers asking for anyone with information about the murder to come forward and call a special hotline which will be monitored around the clock. That number is 1-800-432-9284. Carlisle expects a reward fund will be set up as well.

The last person believed to have seen Levi alive, officials say, was the classmate whose home Levi rode his bike to on the afternoon of Oct. 22. He was reportedly on his way home when he disappeared.

The next morning, Levi’s twin sister, Laci, and their mother, Marilyn Parkman, found the bicycle about a mile from their family’s home. The sixth grader’s body was found in a Dawson County forest around 2:30 p.m. on Thursday.

Although more than a dozen agents from the Georgia Bureau of Investigation, Forsyth County Sheriff’s Department and Dawson County Sheriff’s Department spent their weekend canvassing the boy’s Burruss Mill Road neighborhood for leads in the case, Carlisle said authorities still haven’t been able to talk to the boy’s father, Milton Frady.

That’s because they can’t find him. The 37-year-old has been on the run from police since a bench warrant was issued for his arrest in 1995.

[Continued on page 2A under SEARCH from 1A]

Milton Frady’s conspicuous absence from his son’s funeral Sunday afternoon, and his refusal to help officials in their investigation, continues to fuel speculation about the former Forsyth resident: What, if anything, does he know about his son’s murder?

Milton Frady’s mother says her son loved Levi and could not have harmed him. She says she hopes police find her grandson’s assailant before her son finds the person responsible himself.

And although investigators still haven’t talked to Milton Frady, his mother said she has. In a televised interview Sunday night, Milton’s mother said her son wanted to attend young Levi’s funeral but was afraid officials would arrest him on those earlier charges. The grandmother said her Milton felt it wouldn’t help Levi for him to attend the funeral or for him to go to jail. That’s also the reason, she said, that Milton hasn’t contacted the police.

Dawson County Sheriff Billy Carlisle said Milton Frady can always telephone the sheriff’s department or the tip line if he would like to help them find his son’s killer. “I would encourage him to call us,” Carlisle said.

The fact that he has been a fugitive from Forsyth officials since he failed to appear in court in 1995 doesn’t lessen the flow of questions. The day he failed to appear in Forsyth County Superior Court he was scheduled to answer charges that he committed the offenses of burglary and contributing to the delinquency of a minor. When he didn’t show up, a bench warrant was issued for his arrest.

Whether a weapon or other evidence was found at the crime scene, officials are not saying. They continue to remain tight-lipped about the investigation, saying they fear release of specific information might hamper efforts to bring the murderer to justice.

headline: School ‘still reeling, in shock’ after child’s death
text:
Students and faculty of North Forsyth Middle School tried to get back to business as usual Monday. But it wasn’t easy.

“We are still reeling like this community is,” said principal Jane Fuqua. “We’re in shock.”

The fun and innocence of the students was shattered last week when the body of sixth grader Levi Frady was found in Dawson Forest.

Frady disappeared Wednesday, apparently on his way home from a friend’s house.

On Thursday, family and friends searched frantically in the area surrounding his Burruss Mill home. The only sign of Frady was a bicycle found in a ditch off Little Mill Road, by his twin sister, Laci.

It wasn’t until three hunters stumbled upon the body of the 11-year-old that Frady’s fate was known.

[Continued on page 2A under SCHOOL from 1A]

He was shot to death, the victim of what investigators are calling a murder.

“I really don’t know what to say,” said Fuqua. She and more than 500 students and faculty attended Frady’s funeral Sunday. “But we’re not ready to just bury the issue.”

Three psychologists and the school’s counseling staff returned Monday to help those who wanted and needed to talk about the tragedy.

Parents seemed to have recovered from the initial shock, as was evidenced by the number of children riding the buses.

Fuqua said Friday, it looked like every parent in the school dropped off and picked up their child. Monday, numbers were back up.

But Fuqua said the situation isn’t something that will go away over the course of a weekend.

Regardless of the outcome of law enforcement investigation, the faculty and students will remember Frady every day.

Plans are under way for a permanent memorial on the grounds of North Forsyth Middle School.

Fuqua said there are no definite plans on what the memorial will be, but it will rely heavily on student input.

In the meantime, said Fuqua, the school needs exactly what Frady’s family and the community needs — time and space to heal.

headline: Father of Levi Frady turns himself in
text:
Authorities investigating the murder of 11-year-old Levi Frady may have gotten a break in their investigation.

Although investigators say they still aren’t ready to make an arrest in the case, they finally got a chance to interview the boy’s father, Milton Frady, after he turned himself in to Forsyth authorities on non-related charges Wednesday morning.

Levi was shot to death sometime between 6 p.m. Wednesday, Oct. 22 and 2:30 p.m. the following day. His body was found by a group of Gilmer County deer hunters on state wildlife management land in a wooded Dawson County forest.

While remaining quiet about specifics of the interview, Dawson County Sheriff Billy Carlisle said agents were able to get some helpful information from the long-awaited interview, saying Frady has “cleared up some areas where we had questions.” Agents began following up on those leads Wednesday afternoon.

But as of Wednesday night, Carlisle said an arrest in the case was not imminent, unless other information surfaced. He says no one has been eliminated as a suspect.

Atlanta attorney Michael Hauptman was by his client’s side when Frady was interviewed at the Forsyth County Detention Center by agents from the Georgia Bureau of Investigation and the Forsyth and Dawson counties sheriffs’ departments.

Officials had made it clear they wanted to talk to the 37-year-old construction worker, anxious to find out what — if anything — he might know about his son’s death.

headline: Milton Frady is loving father, says his mother
text:
Milton Frady’s mother Sarah says her son had nothing to do with the murder of his son, sixth grader Levi Frady. During an interview just hours after she brought her son to the Forsyth County Detention Center, Sarah said Milton could not have played a part in her grandson’s death.

“I don’t see how they could suspect him because he was at home,” she said of the night her grandson disappeared. “When he came home from work, Wednesday, Milton was sitting on the porch.” That would have been about 5:15 p.m. she recalled. “He stayed there — he even called” his children’s home that night, Sarah said. “He calls them every night and every morning.”

When he called that night, Sarah said he was told his son had gone to a neighbor’s house. Sarah said he called again the next morning and spoke to Laci but said no one told him Levi had not come home until later that day.

Explaining that Milton loved his children, Sarah said, “He’s been wanting” to come forward since his son was found dead. “He wants the killer found, too.” Sarah said her family wants to help: “That’s why we brought him here,” she said, adding that her son was at the search site Thursday looking for his child with other volunteers.

[Continues as FRADY on page 2A; that continuation is not in this batch.]

headline: Frady reward fund grows
text:
Reward funds which have been set up for information leading to the arrest of the killer of 11-year-old Levi Frady are growing.

During its called meeting Monday, the Forsyth County Board of Commissioners voted unanimously to give another $2000 to the reward fund.

Chairman Bill Jenkins said the board is supporting law enforcement any way they can, and he hopes a reward will help solve the crime.

Gov. Zell Miller allocated $2,000 to the reward fund. Also, Dawson County Sheriff Billy Carlisle said about $3,500 in donations has been received through his office. Forsyth County Sheriff Denny Hendrix said his department has another $7,000 in reward money for what he describes as the department’s top-priority case. Money has been collected from private businesses and concerned citizens.

The father of the Forsyth County Middle School sixth grader could be home Wednesday for the first time in nearly three weeks.

Forsyth County Clerk of Courts Doug Sorrells said the courts are waiting for a motion from Milton Frady’s attorney, Michael Hauptman, for a possible bond hearing Wednesday morning.

Frady turned himself in to the Forsyth County Sheriff’s Office Oct. 29 and has been in custody since.

Frady is being held on bench warrants stemming from a 1994 burglary charge.

But investigators from the Forsyth and Dawson County sheriff’s departments and the Georgia Bureau of Investigation wanted to question Frady about the Oct. 22 murder of his son.

[Continued on page 2A under REWARD from 1A]

Levi Frady was found Oct. 23 in a Dawson County forest where he died from a gunshot wound. Investigators have been looking for his killer.

Milton Frady has been on the run from investigators since the 1994 burglary.

After Levi’s death, the search for his father intensified. Milton’s whereabouts the night of the murder were unknown.

Investigators wanted to know what, if anything, he knew about the case.

While in custody, Frady was questioned by investigators from all three agencies. Dawson County Sheriff Billy Carlisle would not give details about his interview with Frady, but said Frady “cleared up some areas where we had questions.”

None of the representatives from the three investigative agencies will say Frady has been cleared as a suspect. However, all three maintain everyone in and near the family has been questioned and are considered suspects at this time.

The investigation was expanded last week to include anyone traveling through the North Forsyth area near Frady’s home and at Dawson Forest Road and Hwy. 9, near the site where three Gilmer County hunters found the child’s body.

Other hunters on the state wildlife management property that day have been questioned, but the GBI has ruled out an accidental shooting.

Anyone with information should contact the Dawson County tipline at (800) 432-9284, the Forsyth County Crime Stoppers at 888-7308 or the GBI at 535-5423.

headline: Police still looking for second witness in Frady case
text:
After talking to one of the men depicted in two sketches released Wednesday, authorities investigating the murder of Levi Frady still don’t know the identity of the other man in that sketch and now have a third man they would like to locate.

Although they now have a sketch of yet another “potential witness,” it may be early next week before that artist’s rendering is released — if it’s released at all.

Georgia Bureau of Investigation special agent-in-charge Jim Hallman said it may not be necessary to seek the public’s help in identifying the man in the latest drawing. “We have an idea we may know who that man is,” he said.

The latest sketch was prepared Thursday, after a man police talked to during a roadblock came forward to say he had noticed someone who seemed suspicious near the wooded area where the 11-year-old’s body was found.

Hallman said none of the three men depicted in the sketches were seen together and are only considered to be potential witnesses. They are not being characterized as suspects, he said.

As for the man investigators identified and interviewed Wednesday night, Hallman won’t say whether agents learned anything significant and declined to release the man’s name.

He will only say that agents discovered his identity from the “development of a (vehicle) tag number” and went to his home in Forsyth County on the evening the sketch was released.

Hallman said the man had not seen the sketch of himself and was not aware he was being sought in the case.

The as-yet-unidentified white male in the sketch released Nov. 5 was also seen in the area where Levi’s body was found. He was reportedly driving a 1980-85 model medium blue Toyota pickup. Hallman wouldn’t say why the person who described the man considered him to be suspicious.

Hallman said “the case is solvable” and investigators are examining every lead “looking for a break,” saying authorities still want the public’s help. “We would be happy to pay the reward (now more than $15,000) to the person who know something about this killer,” he said.

[Continued on page 2A under FRADY from 1A]

Though television news reports have suggested investigators view revenge against one of Levi’s relatives as a likely motive, Hallman said that report did not come from official sources. He would not discuss possible motives.

Likewise, Hallman would not confirm reports that crime lab technicians found fingerprints at the crime scene, saying that information did not come from authorities. “I haven’t heard anything about prints from the crime lab this week,” he said.

Meanwhile, as of the Forsyth County News’ Friday night deadline, Levi’s father, Milton Frady, remained incarcerated in the county detention center on unrelated charges. Following a Wednesday bond hearing, Frady’s attorney, Michael Hauptman, had said he expected his client would be released by Friday.

At that hearing, Superior Court Judge Frank Mills indicated he would approve a bond — provided Frady could locate an electronic monitoring company willing to fit him with a personal surveillance device. Hauptman said the company which normally provides that service locally doesn’t want to get involved in “high-profile cases” but said he felt certain he could locate another company to take the case.

Mills directed District Attorney Garry Moss to work out the terms of the bond with Hauptman. A previous report erred in stating Judge Stan Gault presided at that hearing. Frady is being held on a 1995 bench warrant for failure to appear to stand trial for his alleged involvement in a 1994 burglary.
extras: Staff Writer. 2A composite-sketch caption: “45- to 55-year-old white male standing 6-foot to 6-foot-1 tall, slim build”. Sketch is a possible witness, not a suspect. The printed quote “person who know something” is retained rather than grammatically rewritten. Adjacent missing-dog reward advertisement excluded.

headline: A grandmother’s plea
text:
TO THE EDITOR:

From the Levi Frady family: We know somebody out there knows something about Levi’s disappearance. It’s so hard to say murder. That’s what it was, murder, and we have to live with that every day of our lives. He was only riding his bike home on Little Mill Road between 6-6:30 p.m. Oct. 22. He was so precious and special but we know that we will never get him back. The only thing we can do for him now is to make sure nobody else has to suffer what Levi went through, at least by this person or persons. It could have been anyone’s child and we don’t want anyone to go through what we’re going through. We didn’t know a person could hurt so bad and still be alive. With God’s help, we will go on but we will never stop hunting his murderer. So please, please, somebody help us. If the reward won’t make your come forth, maybe our cries will.

The heartbroken family of Levi,
Janice Hamby, Levi’s grandmother

(If you have information about the Frady case, you are asked to call the hotline established at 800-432-9284; the Georgia Bureau of Investigation at 535-5423 or the Forsyth County Crimestopper line at 888-7308.)

headline: Father of murdered child out on bond
text:
Following a week of negotiations, the father of 11-year-old murder victim Levi Frady was released from the Forsyth County Detention Center Monday.

Superior Court Judge Frank Mills ordered Milton Frady to wear an electronic monitoring system and remain at the Nichols Road home of his parents, Lamar and Sara Frady, unless appearing in court.

Frady turned himself in to the Sheriff’s Office Oct. 29. He was wanted for failing to appear in court in 1995 to answer to charges of burglary and contributing to the delinquency of a minor.

Investigators from the Forsyth and Dawson county sheriff’s departments and the Georgia Bureau Investigation wanted to question him about the Oct. 22 murder of his son, whose body was found Oct. 23 in a Dawson County forest by three hunters from Gilmer County. Levi disappeared Oct. 22 and family and neighbors searched north Forsyth County for the boy.

[Continued on page 2A under BOND from 1A]

Milton Frady did not attend the Nov. 2 funeral of his son. At the time, Sara Frady said her son was worried about being arrested for the outstanding warrants.

Milton Frady was questioned by investigators after turning himself in, but could not be released as a condition of his bond until a company was found to provide an electronic monitoring system.

Milton Frady’s attorney, Michael Hauptman, said many of the companies were wary of taking on a high-profile case.

Sentinel Monitoring Corporation, a Marietta-based firm, agreed to provide security late last week.

Milton Frady will wear an ankle bracelet which is wired directly to the security company. In addition, surveillance cameras will be set up in and around the residence.

Frady was also ordered to post a $22,400 bond and pay for the cost of deputies transporting him home. No court date has been set for the 1995 charges.

Meanwhile, authorities say they are still pursuing leads in their investigation into the murder of Levi Frady.

The second man in the sketch police released last week remains unidentified. Investigators say the man is not considered a suspect but is thought to be a potential witness.

They said they simply want to talk with him to see if he has any information.

The man in a third artist sketch, which was never released to the public, has been identified. Special Agent in Charge of the Gainesville Georgia Bureau of Investigation office, Jim Hallman, said agents interviewed the man over the weekend and are pursuing leads from information he provided.

Hallman declined to identify the man, who was seen in the wooded area near the location where Levi was murdered. The description of the man was provided by a citizen police talked to during a roadblock in the area last week.

“The case is still progressing,” Hallman said. “We’ve got a number of leads remaining to check, and we’re doing that as quickly as possible.”
extras: Staff Writer. “Nov. 2 funeral” is clearly printed, not an OCR correction; conflicts with earlier scheduling/reporting and remains unresolved. Sara and Sarah spellings retained separately pending identity review. No case photograph/caption. Statement about future monitoring/cameras is not proof of installation.
